admitted.text: Pace seems committed to letting Vee choose each step, even when waiting costs him.
admitted.detail_quote: that was what he did, he backed off and let her decide

admitted.text: His idea of consent reads as sincere and close to a principle he lives by.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: His tenderness comes with an appetite to watch, and the game reads as his idea as much as Randi's.
admitted.detail_quote: He had been reading her more than them by the end of it.

admitted.text: Pace reads as extraordinarily attentive, making care concrete through food, warmth, craft, and remembered detail.
admitted.detail_quote: He had sliced it thin because she would eat thin slices and would not eat thick ones

admitted.text: By his own account, fear is what keeps him from saying he loves her.
admitted.detail_quote: He had hurt her because he was afraid of how much she could hurt him.

admitted.text: He reads as oddly blind to Randi's pain even while he reads her body closely.
admitted.detail_quote: He did not know what he had done. He looked for it, back through the evening from the gravel forward, and it was not there.

admitted.text: He seems to carry an old wound from a relationship that began when he was a boy.
admitted.detail_quote: He had handed her the thing that had hurt him and named it luck.

admitted.text: Even in memory, she reads as the formative wound in Pace's life, an older woman whose departure taught him to equate spoken love with unbearable loss.
admitted.detail_quote: She had been his tutor, then his best friend, his first girlfriend, his first lover, his first love.

admitted.text: The relationship Pace calls luck reads, through Vee, as something darker.
admitted.detail_quote: The word for it started to form in her, the clean ugly grown-up word

admitted.text: His silence about his family reads as hiding a deeper break.
admitted.detail_quote: I don't go back.

admitted.text: His attention to Vee's friends reads as real care for her whole life, not only her body.
admitted.detail_quote: Bring Theo," Pace said, and reached for the next pan.

admitted.text: From the first chapter she reads as someone who hides her real self behind a polished face.
admitted.detail_quote: The face took the being-looked-at, the being-wanted, the being-touched, and none of it reached any further than the face, because the face was not her.

admitted.text: She seems to hurt herself quietly whenever her feelings rise.
admitted.detail_quote: set the sharp inner edge of the cap under her thumbnail and pressed — slow and steady, down into the nail bed, where it would hurt

admitted.text: Her coaching of Vee reads as warm and manipulative at the same time.
admitted.detail_quote: I know exactly what I'm doing. I have always known what I'm doing.

admitted.text: She seems to love Vee without calculation and to be terrified of losing her.
admitted.detail_quote: I keep waiting to get bored of her — I get bored of everybody — and it doesn't come.

admitted.text: Randi seems terrified that speaking plainly will destroy the friendship that currently lets her keep Vee close.
admitted.detail_quote: She was not brave enough to lose her.

admitted.text: Her jealousy of Pace over Vee reads as growing.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend, and you're in no hurry, and I can't think why you would be.

admitted.text: She seems trapped by her family and her sorority, and the right life feels like nothing to her.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi, relying on her sorority practice, returned the smile warmly and hugged him, eating her revulsion.

admitted.text: her long silence after the green-panties morning reads as retreat from feeling too much, not from losing interest
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: reads as the flawlessness that leaves Randi cold — everything done well and nothing reaching her
admitted.detail_quote: This was the best the acceptable world could do for her. Not a poor version of it. The best: a faultless man asleep in a faultless room

admitted.text: She reads as long underfed, in both food and desire, and as finally waking to it.
admitted.detail_quote: Like my mouth had been asleep since I was born and nobody told me. Like I'd been eating with the sound off.

admitted.text: Her mother's shame seems to sit inside her own desire and to drive it.
admitted.detail_quote: she could not find the seam between the heat and the shame because there was no seam, they ran on the same wire

admitted.text: She seems to explain away her attraction to Randi as fast as she feels it.
admitted.detail_quote: It's a French thing, she does the kiss-kiss, she's been everywhere, that's all it is, that's just how women like her say goodbye.

admitted.text: Her need for a name for what she and Pace are reads as the center of her unrest.
admitted.detail_quote: He had the whole of her, and what she had of him she could not have held up to anyone, could not have proved.

admitted.text: Her loyalty reads as a quiet kindness: she keeps the PPP secret to shield Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: the kindest thing a friend could do was not make her carry it in front of anyone

admitted.text: She has started telling small lies to protect her secrets, even to Cassie.
admitted.detail_quote: What she kept was the middle. She lifted it out clean as she went, the way a ladle takes soup from the pot

admitted.text: Vee reads as capable of self-deception when happiness depends on preserving a preferred version of events.
admitted.detail_quote: it settled somewhere under the affection and stayed, minor-key, waiting.

admitted.text: reads as braver than she knows — the coat, the entrance, the pointing finger are her own nerve, not anyone's script
admitted.detail_quote: She took a breath, and made the second step long.

admitted.text: She reads as steadily loyal and protective of Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend

admitted.text: She seems to sense something off about Randi from the start.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't take the bit's open door — didn't do the *oh, mine's a whole thing too* that the bit was built to be answered with

admitted.text: She reads as the one person blunt enough to name what Pace's silence costs.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't want him, she wasn't impressed by him, and she'd say so to his face; she just liked him and gave him hell.

admitted.text: Behind her warmth she reads as a watchful enforcer of the house's rules.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: reads as the calm witness, the one who tracks Vee's story in installments and sees the shape of it
admitted.detail_quote: Meg was the calm one, dark-haired and level

admitted.text: reads as warmth without depth of sight — cheerful, loyal, largely unaware of what she's not seeing
admitted.detail_quote: Don't do anything I wouldn't do,

admitted.text: The bench: a hidden machine of exposure that waits for its next use, perhaps for Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: Tomorrow he would put the top back on and the bench would be a long table again

admitted.text: The deadbolt: Randi locking her true self away.
admitted.detail_quote: she always locked it behind her, first thing, before anything else

admitted.text: The white-gold bracelet: a locked restraint that seems tied to her family's money.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi felt her own bracelet, plain white gold, locked on her wrist, and kept it out of the light.

admitted.text: The green panties: Vee's gift turned into a token of Randi's grief and possessiveness.
admitted.detail_quote: Her hand with the green in it stayed flat against his chest, and he could feel the satin there between her palm and his skin

admitted.text: The burgundy dress: being seen and made for exactly as she is.
admitted.detail_quote: He didn't make this *for* you," she said. "He made it *to* you.

admitted.text: Pace’s flannel shirt: material intimacy failing when its warmth proves to be Vee’s own heat returned
admitted.detail_quote: the heat in the shirt was her own, given back. He wasn't in it.

admitted.text: The drawer: a place made for Vee instead of a word spoken to her.
admitted.detail_quote: He'd folded his whole ordered self down into a single drawer. He'd given her the top one.

admitted.text: Simpson's paradox: the same facts can tell opposite stories depending on how they are grouped.
admitted.detail_quote: Each year on its own, the first man is the better hitter. Put the two years together and the second man is.

admitted.text: Crackers and a meal: Vee's "I love you" in disguise.
admitted.detail_quote: I had been eating crackers my whole life," she said. "And you fed me a meal.

admitted.text: The right-angle mark: separate desires or people becoming intelligible only when placed into a new relation
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: The pool: a space where Vee’s watched and judged body becomes functional, private, and wholly hers
admitted.detail_quote: Nobody up there could see her. Nobody down here wanted anything.

admitted.text: Pace’s scar: a sealed history held beneath intimacy, with touch allowed before explanation
admitted.detail_quote: the one she had found that first night and traced and never been told about

admitted.text: the MIRA outlier: reads as the one data point that can't be smoothed — the rotten fact under the glamour
admitted.detail_quote: the biggest one, off on its own in the white

admitted.text: the sweetness on her lip she never touched: reads as the truth already present before Vee admits wanting Randi
admitted.detail_quote: there was a thread of sweetness, sugar and butter and something warm under it, the glaze of a pastry she had never once touched

admitted.text: Will Vee find out that she was chosen in a game Randi and Pace began together?
admitted.detail_quote: She had asked for something different with her eyes on the table.

admitted.text: Will Pace ever say aloud that he loves Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: She had said her best sentence. He had not said the sentence back.

admitted.text: What is the story behind Pace's scar?
admitted.detail_quote: He kept it there under his, on the thing he wasn't going to tell her about yet

admitted.text: What happened between Pace and his parents?
admitted.detail_quote: He had taken his mother out of the answer. Vee let him.

admitted.text: Will Vee realize what, or whom, she tasted on Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: Under the tidy explanation, fainter, the other question kept its small light on: how many times, and how carefully, and had there always been

admitted.text: Will Randi choose her place in the sorority or Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: You've got a position in this house, and you've got her. You need to choose.

admitted.text: Will Randi ever tell Vee what she feels, or keep waiting for Vee to get there herself?
admitted.detail_quote: Let Vee arrive at it on her own.

admitted.text: Why does Randi hide where she comes from behind an accent Vee takes for European?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had something in her mouth that wasn't from anywhere near here — the esses ran a half-beat long, and the a's came up arched and lifted

admitted.text: When Pace gathers all of Vee's people in one room, will what he and Randi share come out?
admitted.detail_quote: and there was something in his face she'd have called happiness if he'd let it any further out.
